_about: Every visible thing, by id (D30). The game loads game/assets/models/<id>.glb when it exists, else a labelled box. Briefs: docs/MODELS_AND_VARIETY.md section 1. Status: box | modelled.

props.name: The service van
props.what: Your first company vehicle: a second-hand cream panel van with a rust-red stripe, a roof rack for the ladder and a fold-down tailboard for the drum, toolbox and modems. Front faces -Z.
props.pivot: ground under the middle of the body (x 0, z 0)
props.charm: A hand-painted TELO on the side in slightly uneven letters, over the ghost of the previous owner's bakery name.
props.nodes: Wheels are separate objects named wheel-fl, wheel-fr, wheel-rl, wheel-rr with their origin at the hub, so the game can spin them.

takes.plain: Cream panel van, rust-red stripe, chrome bumpers, round headlamps.
takes.bodge: A roof rack made of scaffold pole and rope.

props.name: The switchboard
props.what: Your hand-built distribution board on the room's back wall: subscriber terminals with paper tags down the left, Board ports with lamps down the right, a tool shelf along the bottom. The centrepiece of the room.
props.charm: Pencilled names and crossings-out straight on the plywood beside the tags, and a coffee ring near the TEST switch.

takes.plain: Varnished plywood, brass hardware screwed on by hand, a shelf from an offcut.
takes.old: What you started from: a telex repair shop's spare backboard, old screw holes and a faded stencil.
takes.bodge: The upgrade panel bolted on slightly crooked with odd screws; a strip of gaffer tape holding a tag strip.

props.rules: Rows are not fixed: row pitch is 0.95 / (rows + 1) down from row-top. Terminals, ports, tags and lamps are separate props placed per row, so the board model is the backing, shelf, stencils and hardware only.
props.replaces: SwitchboardStation.cs BuildStatic (the Ply boxes and labels)

props.name: Subscriber terminal
props.what: Where a customer's pair arrives on the board. Two brass screw posts; a jumper's near end is wound on here.
props.charm: One screw head with a slot cut crooked.
states: loose (a jumper half off the post)

takes.plain: Two polished brass posts on a small bakelite block.
takes.old: Green with verdigris, a post that turns forever.
takes.bodge: A bent nail with the wire twisted round it.

props.name: Board port
props.what: A jack that leads to one of the Board's ports. A jumper's far end plugs in here. Spare ports (S1, S2) are nickel instead of brass.
props.charm: The number stamped into the collar, not printed.

takes.plain: Brass jack in a round collar.
takes.old: A jack with a cracked collar and a scorch mark: the bad port.
takes.bodge: A jack held in with a blob of solder and hope.

props.name: Port lamp
props.what: A small jewelled lamp beside each port. Burns while that subscriber is on the Board; shows test results.
props.charm: A faceted glass jewel cap, like an old panel lamp.

takes.plain: Clear faceted jewel over a bulb.
takes.old: Jewel yellowed with age, the colour slightly off.
takes.bodge: A bare bulb with no cap.

props.rules: The colour comes from the material at run time; the model is the cap and bezel only.

props.name: Paper tag
props.what: A strip of card naming the subscriber on each terminal row. It can smudge until it needs a tone-probe.
props.charm: Handwritten name, a drawing pin at the left end.

takes.bodge: A torn corner of an envelope, written on in pencil.

props.rules: Height follows the row pitch (at most 0.04). The text stays a Label3D on the text anchor.

props.name: Jumper wire end
props.what: The ends of a jumper wire. The wire itself stays drawn in code (it sags between any two points); only its ends and the coils on the hook are models.
props.charm: A coloured sleeve on each end, slightly too long.

takes.plain: Moulded plug with a coloured sleeve.
takes.old: Grey cloth-covered wire, frayed at the end: the hot-wire option.
takes.bodge: Bare twisted copper, no plug at all.

props.replaces: SwitchboardStation.cs AddWire ends and hand Wire box

props.name: Jumper hook
props.what: Two brass hooks under the board: new coloured jumpers on the left, salvaged old wire on the right.
props.charm: 'OLD' scratched into the right-hand hook's bar.

takes.plain: Brass cup hooks with neat coils hanging.

props.name: Tone probe
props.what: A yellow probe that finds a pair by its tone. Used to read a smudged tag.
props.charm: A strip of tape on the handle: 'PROPERTY OF' and the name scratched out.

takes.old: Yellow worn to cream where the thumb goes.
takes.bodge: A probe held together with an elastic band.

props.name: Lineman's test handset
props.what: A chunky handset with crocodile clips, for testing a port before trusting it.
props.charm: Chipped paint and a curly cord ending in two clips.

takes.plain: Black handset, coiled cord, red and black clips.
takes.bodge: An ordinary phone handset with the clips soldered on.

props.name: TEST knife switch
props.what: The big switch that tries every new line at once: live, dead or crossed.
props.charm: 'TEST' hand-painted in white, a little drip under the T.

takes.plain: Slate base, brass blade, wooden handle.
takes.old: A switch salvaged from a shop's fuse board.
takes.bodge: A light switch screwed on sideways.

props.name: Upgrade panel
props.what: The $120 panel that takes the board from 8 subscribers to 16. Shown as a price sign until bought, then as the extra rows.
props.charm: A paper price label still stuck on after fitting.

takes.old: A second-hand panel in a different wood.

props.name: Lines-in rack
props.what: Beside the switchboard: one lamp per line into the Board, and a tally card of tonight's callers and engaged tones.
props.charm: A tally card clipped on with a bulldog clip, five-bar gates in pencil.

takes.plain: A grey scavenged relay rack, neat card slots.
takes.old: A rack with a missing slot cover.
takes.bodge: Cards wedged into a cutlery drawer.

props.name: Line card
props.what: A circuit card you buy at Sol's ($60), carry from the van and slot into the rack: one more line into the Board.
props.charm: A handwritten serial number sticker and one chip with a paper label.

takes.plain: Green board, black chips, gold edge.
takes.old: A second-hand card, a burnt resistor.
takes.bodge: A card with a component held in with a blob of putty.
